definitions.explanation: Someone who has more experience in a group, school, or workplace.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}に{相談|そうだん}しました。
{彼|かれ}は{大学|だいがく}の{先輩|せんぱい}です。
{先輩|せんぱい}が{教|おし}えてくれた。
{先輩|せんぱい}はとても{親切|しんせつ}で、いつも{助|たす}けてくれる。
examples.english: My senior is very kind and always helps me.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{先輩|せんぱい}に{仕事|しごと}のやり{方|かた}を{教|おし}えてもらって、とても{勉強|べんきょう}になった。
examples.english: My senior colleague taught me how to do the work, and I learned a lot.

notes:
{先輩|せんぱい} refers to someone senior to you in age, experience, or position within a group, school, or workplace.

CULTURAL SIGNIFICANCE:
The {先輩|せんぱい}・{後輩|こうはい} relationship is fundamental to Japanese social structure, especially in schools, clubs, and companies.

USAGE:
- As a noun: {先輩|せんぱい}に{聞|き}く (ask a senior)
- As an address: 〇〇{先輩|せんぱい} (Senior ~, used as a title)
- With possessive: {大学|だいがく}の{先輩|せんぱい} (university senior)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {先輩|せんぱい}に{相談|そうだん}する: to consult with a senior
- {先輩|せんぱい}から{教|おそ}わる: to learn from a senior

RELATED:
- {後輩|こうはい}: junior (opposite)
- {同期|どうき}: same year/cohort
